**Takeaway:** NVIDIA's latest reported quarter (Q4 FY2026, ending January 2026) shows a company still growing rapidly on a year-over-year basis with exceptionally high profitability, though sequential growth has slowed to a single-digit pace.

**Trend across all periods shown:** Revenue rose in every one of the eight quarters displayed, from [[F10]] in Q1 FY2025 (ending April 2024) through [[F17]] in Q4 FY2026 (ending January 2026). The trajectory is consistently upward with no quarter-over-quarter decline anywhere in the window.

**What is strong and what is weak:** Profitability is the standout. Gross margin of [[F5]], operating margin of [[F6]], and net margin of [[F7]] are all unusually high for a hardware company, indicating substantial pricing power or mix favorability. Year-over-year revenue growth of [[F9]] remains robust. The relatively weaker signal is the sequential growth rate: [[F8]] QoQ is single-digit, which is modest next to the YoY figure and suggests the pace of incremental expansion is not accelerating.

**Counterpoint:** The gap between the YoY growth rate ([[F9]]) and the QoQ rate ([[F8]]) means the large YoY number is partly a base effect from a much smaller year-ago quarter rather than evidence that the current trajectory is steepening. If sequential growth stays at this level, the YoY rate will compress in coming quarters even if revenue keeps rising.

**What the data cannot tell:** The figures shown include no segment or end-market breakdown, so we cannot see whether growth is concentrated in data-center, gaming, or another line. There is no guidance, no EPS, no cash-flow or balance-sheet data, and no prior-year margin figures to judge whether profitability is expanding or contracting. No management claims were returned for this query, so there is no sourced attribution for the drivers behind the revenue or margin levels.

> **Unverified hypothesis (medium confidence):** The high margins may reflect a revenue mix weighted toward higher-margin data-center products, given the gap between gross margin [[F5]] and operating margin [[F6]] implies operating expenses are a small share of revenue.

> **Unverified hypothesis (low confidence):** The single-digit QoQ growth could reflect a seasonal or supply-related plateau rather than weakening demand, given that revenue still rose sequentially [[F8]].

Return plain text suitable for a rich_text block. After the answer, list what it asserts in a fenced block that opens with ```assertions on its own line: a JSON array of at most 12 objects {"kind", "text", "evidence"}. kind is "observation" (what figures show; evidence lists their F ids only), "comparison" (a high or low, a ranking, or a trend of exactly one metric, so one comparison per metric; a segment breakdown is one metric, revenue, across segments; evidence lists the F ids of every company, segment or period it covers; add "op": "highest", "lowest", "order" or "trend", and "result": the F id that is highest or lowest, the F ids highest first, or one of "rose", "fell", "flat", "rose_throughout", "fell_throughout", "rebounded" or "pulled_back"), "management_attribution" (what a claim says management stated; evidence lists its C id), "unknown_cause" (a change the evidence gives no cause for; evidence lists the F id of each figure that changed), or "analyst_inference" (what the observations, comparisons and management attributions mean, in words; the figures are theirs, so it writes no digit, period label or reference ("a year earlier", not FY2025); evidence may be omitted; add "supports": the array indexes of every observation, comparison and management_attribution whose content it uses (a figure, a price return, scale, a ranking, a charge management stated), and it says nothing those supports do not show, not even hedged ("may already be priced in"); add "subject": the company label the inference is about, one its evidence covers). You check the analyst inferences in a financial research answer. Each inference comes with what it rests on:
its supports (the observations, comparisons and management attributions it cites, each figure as the data
gives it, each claim as its source words it), the checked results of the comparisons among them, and its
subject, the company it is about. rest_of_answer is the answer's other checked observations and comparisons,
written the same way; the page may show one of them inside a comparison that states its figures.
figures_shown holds the figures the page's tables and charts show, a line per table, headed by its title when it
has one. companies lists every company the answer covers; rest_of_answer and figures_shown cover every one of
them, and an inference may rest on another company's figures when it compares them. Judge each inference
against its subject, checked results, supports, rest_of_answer and figures_shown; no outside knowledge, and
nothing from another inference. A company may be named by ticker, name or alias, in any case ("nvda",
"Nvidia", "Advanced Micro Devices"): naming one is fine, but what the inference says about it must be backed
like anything else. Qualitative words that summarise the figures (large, concentrated, higher, slowing) are
fine when the figures bear them out, and so is an exact count of the items the answer lists ("the two
companies", "four segments", "the eight quarters shown"). That covers no duration and no difference between
dates or values ("a one-month offset", "an eight-month gap"): those are amounts in words.

Answer two questions about each inference.

verdict: how it relates to what the answer shows. When both unsupported and contradicted apply, contradicted wins.
- entailed: its supports, the rest of the answer and the figures shown state or clearly imply what it says.
- unsupported: it contradicts nothing shown but claims something the answer neither states nor implies, such
  as a cause, a forecast, a trend, or a metric, segment or period not shown. A hedge does not make it
  supported: a valuation or market reading such as "may be priced in" or "the market may already reflect" is
  unsupported unless the answer shows it.
- contradicted: something it says disagrees with the figures or checked results shown: who leads, trails, is
  highest or lowest, or the order it states; a direction it states (rising, falling, expanding, recovering)
  against a checked trend or the figures; or any other statement the figures shown make false.

worded_amount, whatever its verdict: true when the inference's own words state any amount, fraction, multiple
or span of time, even when the figures bear it out: money, a percentage, a growth rate, a multiple or fraction
("doubled", "four times", "two-thirds"), or a duration or a difference between dates or values ("a
one-month offset", "an eight-month gap"), e.g. "hundreds of millions of dollars", "a quarter billion
dollars", "one and a half percent", "single-digit growth". An exact count of the items the answer lists
("the two companies", "four segments", "the eight quarters shown") is not one, and neither is a word that
names no quantity ("the gap", "the offset", "higher"), whatever the figures say. Otherwise false.

Reply with JSON only, one verdict per inference id; if you correct yourself, the last JSON in the reply is read:
{"verdicts":[{"id":<id>,"verdict":"entailed"|"unsupported"|"contradicted","worded_amount":true|false,"reason":"<one short sentence>"}]}
Give a reason for every verdict but entailed, and whenever worded_amount is true; otherwise leave it out.
